layoutProps.lead: You will brew hundreds of pour-overs. Here is the bar's recipe, and what to change when a cup tastes wrong.

props.stem: Before you start: your pour-over tastes sour and thin. What would you change first?

options.feedback: A darker roast changes the coffee, not the brew: the same mistake would make it sour too. The lesson shows what to change.

options.text: Add more water to the cup
options.feedback: More water would make it thinner still. Keep your answer in mind: the lesson shows what to change.
A good instinct. You will see why below: a sour cup is one the water passed through too fast.

props.alt: A pour-over station: a grinder, a paper dripper on a glass carafe on a scale, and a kettle.
props.prompt: Follow the bar's recipe, step by step.

items.title: Grind fresh
items.markdown: Weigh 20 g of beans and grind them medium-fine, like coarse sand, just before you brew: ground coffee goes stale in minutes.

items.title: Rinse the filter
items.markdown: Rinse the paper filter with hot water and pour that water away. It warms the carafe and takes away the taste of paper.

items.title: Let it bloom
items.markdown: Add the coffee, set the scale to zero and pour about 40 g of water. Wait 30 seconds while the grounds bubble and let out their gas.

items.title: Pour in circles
items.markdown: Pour slowly in circles up to 320 g of water, at about 94 °C. The water should drain in about three minutes; then serve.

props.markdown: Brewing dissolves part of the ground coffee in water: that is **extraction**. Acids dissolve first, then sugars, then bitter compounds. Too little extraction and the cup is **sour** and thin; too much, and it is **bitter** and dry. Grind, time, temperature and ratio all move it.

props.prompt: For your shift: what to do when a cup tastes wrong.

items.title: Sour and thin
items.markdown: Under-extracted: the water passed too fast, or it was too cool. Grind finer, and check the kettle is at temperature.

items.title: Bitter and dry
items.markdown: Over-extracted: the grind is too fine or the brew too long. Grind coarser, so that the water drains in about three minutes.

items.title: Weak and watery
items.markdown: Too little coffee for the water. Check the dose on the scale: 20 g of coffee for 320 g of water.

items.title: The water drains slowly
items.markdown: The grind is too fine, or fine particles are clogging the filter. Grind coarser, and pour more gently.

props.stem: Our recipe is 1 part coffee to 16 parts water. How many grams of water for 20 g of coffee?

feedback.correct: Yes: 20 × 16 = 320 g. That is why we brew on a scale: you pour by weight, not by eye.
feedback.incorrect: Each gram of coffee takes 16 grams of water: multiply the coffee by 16.

misconceptions.feedback: You added 20 and 16. The ratio is a multiplication: 16 grams of water for each gram of coffee.
You divided 20 by 16. Each gram of coffee takes 16 grams of water: multiply instead.

props.stem: Complete the rule of thumb you will use at the bar.
props.markdown: A sour cup is [[under-extracted|underextracted|under extracted]]: grind [[finer|more finely]]. A bitter cup is [[over-extracted|overextracted|over extracted]]: grind [[coarser|more coarsely]].

feedback.correct: That is the rule: sour means too little extraction, so slow the water down with a finer grind; bitter means too much, so grind coarser.
feedback.incorrect: Think of the order things dissolve in: acids first, bitter compounds last. Which cup stopped too early, and which went on too long?

props.title: Do
props.markdown:
- Keep beans in their bag, valve and seal closed
- Store them cool, dry and dark
- Grind just before you brew

props.title: Don't
props.markdown:
- Keep them in the fridge
- Leave the grinder's hopper full overnight
- Grind the day's coffee in the morning

props.prompt: Say what each word means before you turn the card.

items.title: Bloom
items.markdown: The first small pour that wets the grounds and lets their gas escape, so that the rest of the water reaches the coffee evenly.

items.title: Extraction
items.markdown: The part of the ground coffee that dissolves in the water: too little tastes sour, too much tastes bitter.

items.title: Ratio
items.markdown: Coffee to water, by weight. Ours is 1 to 16: 20 g of coffee for 320 g of water.

items.title: Drawdown
items.markdown: The time the water takes to drain through the bed of coffee. About three minutes for our pour-over.
